brief.headline: Push PIK PLASTICS to match our best bottle price (₹7.62/NOS) and save ₹8.48 L/year — we already pay less to TPAC and Suraj, so they can meet it.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match the ₹7.62/NOS we pay TPAC Packaging for the same 250 ml amber PET bottle, and bring the second SKU down to ₹5.24/NOS (our Suraj price).
priceAsk.basis: We are paying ₹8.48 L more per year to PIK than the lowest prices we already get from other suppliers for the same rigid plastic packaging items. The biggest gap is the PET bottle: they charge ₹8.49/NOS when TPAC delivers at ₹7.62/NOS (11.5% cheaper). No reason to pay more for identical goods.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 days — it's not our worst term, and we have no signal they need faster cash.

brief.financialLeverage: PIK PLASTICS publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we build our case purely on the prices we already pay elsewhere and on lining up backup suppliers. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend is real money to a private converter, so they'll listen. Without their financials we won't push payment terms, but the price ask stands on its own: we have proof we can buy the same bottles cheaper today.

evidence.point: We pay PIK ₹8.48 L more per year than the best prices we get from other suppliers for the same packaging
The 250 ml amber PET bottle costs us ₹8.49/NOS from PIK but only ₹7.62/NOS from TPAC — an 11.5% gap
The second bottle (BRUT 250 ml) is ₹5.38/NOS from PIK and ₹5.24/NOS from Suraj — 2.6% cheaper at Suraj
Market research shows a typical 28 mm PP cap trades at ₹0.85–0.95 per piece, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
evidence.figure: ask band ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict MARKET-FAIR with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

evidence.point: We spend ₹1.92 Cr a year with PIK — a meaningful customer for a private converter

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, makes pharma bottles and caps — a proven second source we can move volume to if PIK won't match our TPAC price

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd (listed PET bottle specialist)
alternates.why: Pearlpet brand, direct fit for our PET bottles — a credible alternate to qualify for the amber bottle line

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed, rigid-plastic leader)
alternates.why: Strong, profitable listed company covering pharma bottles and closures — robust backup for the full rigid-packaging basket

risks: PIK's financials are private, so we can't see if they're struggling or healthy — watch for any supply hiccups and don't squeeze so hard we risk continuity without a qualified second source in place first.

We have four strong alternates identified but none are RFQ-ready today — before we push PIK to the wall, get at least one (Manjushree or Pearl) qualified and priced so we have a real walk-away option.
The 11.5% gap on the amber bottle is large — if PIK insists their spec or lead-time justifies it, ask them to prove the difference in writing and then test the claim with TPAC.
If they agree to match ₹7.62 but want a volume commitment in return, confirm we can actually shift that tonnage from TPAC without breaking our supply chain before you nod.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're reviewing all our packaging suppliers, and the numbers show we're paying you ₹8.48 lakh more per year than our best prices for the same bottles — let's talk about how we close that gap.
